TimePeriod: Ancient (Genesis 10 era); Jeremiah's oracle against Babylon
Region: A northern kingdom summoned against Babylon (Jeremiah 51:27); the precise location is debated
History: Ashkenaz, son of Gomer, is named in the Table of Nations (Genesis 10:3). The name returns once, in Jeremiah 51:27, where the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz are called together against Babylon (Jeremiah spells the name Ashchenaz). The later Jewish association of Ashkenaz with Germany belongs to a much later period and is not the biblical identification.
Culture: Nothing distinct is recorded of Ashkenazite culture beyond a kingdom able to answer Jeremiah's summons.
Religion: Nothing distinct is recorded of Ashkenazite religion.
BibleConnection: Ashkenaz appears twice: a Gomerite name in the Table of Nations, then a northern kingdom in Jeremiah's oracle of Babylon's fall.
